headline: THE ASHCOMBE HOUR WANTS YOUR CANDIDATE FOR A FULL HOUR
body: A local politics podcast with a startlingly large audience and a host who does actual research. An hour is a long time. Your candidate has not been interesting for an hour at any point in his life.

responses.label: Accept the invitation
responses.hint: An hour is a very long time to fill.
responses.flavour: You accept before you can think better of it. They record on Thursday. You have one afternoon to get him ready.

responses.label: Politely decline
responses.flavour: The host reads your decline statement aloud on air, slowly, in full, and then leaves a pause long enough to park a bus in.

headline: ONE AFTERNOON. WHAT DO YOU PREP HIM ON?
body: He will be asked about the railway, the hospital, and — because the host is good at this — his own record. You can only drill one thing properly.

responses.label: Railway policy, line by line
responses.hint: Dry, thorough, aimed squarely at the commute.
responses.flavour: He is word-perfect on the 07:42 and visibly bored by minute nine. The commuter forums call it 'the most substantial interview of the campaign', which is not a compliment about the campaign.

responses.label: Warmth, family, the personal story
responses.flavour: He talks about his father's allotment for eleven uninterrupted minutes. Two listeners write in to say they cried. One writes in to complain about the allotment waiting list.

responses.label: No prep. Let him be himself
responses.hint: Unfiltered. Could be electric. Could be a clip.
responses.flavour: He is loose, funny, and entirely unmanaged. Forty seconds of it are already a sound-on-loop with 200,000 views and a caption you would not have chosen.

headline: CANDIDATE PHOTOGRAPHED LEAVING CASINO AT 4AM
body: The Ashcombe Echo has a picture. In it, your candidate is squinting, holding a complimentary tote bag, and appears to be explaining something important to a bollard. The photographer has three more and is asking what they're worth.

responses.label: Deny everything
responses.flavour: You state that the candidate was at a constituency fundraiser. The Echo prints the photo next to your statement, which is the worst possible layout.

responses.label: Half-apology, full contrition tour
responses.flavour: The candidate is very sorry that people feel the way they do about the thing that did not technically happen.

responses.label: Bury it under a bigger story
responses.flavour: You leak a completely unrelated planning scandal to a rival paper. It works. It works so well that nobody can remember what your candidate stands for either.
